findings.summary: The table name is checked with match() on an unanchored pattern, so any name that merely starts with an identifier passes and the rest goes into every statement as SQL.
Retention keeps the job's rows only if they are among the newest keep runs of all jobs, so a busy job deletes a quieter job's history.
The duration uses timedelta.seconds, which drops fractions of a second (and whole days), instead of total_seconds().
last_success orders by id ascending, so it returns the oldest successful run rather than the newest.

The table-name pattern uses the range A-z, which also covers [ \ ] ^ and the backtick, SQLite's identifier quote characters, so a table name that is not a plain identifier passes the check and its quoting goes into every statement.
